title: Targeted Philanthropy: Evidence from M&As
abstract: ABSTRACT I show how firms optimize the allocation of charitable funds around investments that require external stakeholder support, such as mergers and acquisitions. Acquirers increase donations to target‐related charities before making a takeover offer, but scale funds back after withdrawing from a deal. Firms redistribute funds from nontakeover‐related areas to target insider–affiliated charities, employee communities, and counties with a regulatory presence. Targeted donations that encourage blockholder reciprocity and employee commitment are associated with better deal performance through decreased merger premiums and lower integration costs. Overall, the results highlight firms’ use of philanthropy to manage stakeholder relations in takeover decisions.
summary: ABSTRACT I show how firms optimize the allocation of charitable funds around investments that require external stakeholder support, such as mergers and acquisitions.
finding: Targeted donations that encourage blockholder reciprocity and employee commitment are associated with better deal performance through decreased merger premiums and lower integration costs.

title: Flow‐Driven ESG Returns
abstract: ABSTRACT I show that the recent returns to environmental, social, and governance (ESG) investing are strongly driven by price impact from flows toward ESG portfolios. Using data on trades, I estimate the market's ability to accommodate ESG flows, which is given by the elasticity of substitution between ESG and other stocks. I show that every dollar flowing toward a representative ESG portfolio increases the market value of ESG stocks by $0.8. The growing institutional flows into the ESG portfolio are the main driver of ESG returns and have caused an annual flow‐driven return of 1.9%. In the absence of flows, ESG stocks would not have outperformed the market from 2012 to 2023.
summary: ABSTRACT I show that the recent returns to environmental, social, and governance (ESG) investing are strongly driven by price impact from flows toward ESG portfolios.
finding: I show that every dollar flowing toward a representative ESG portfolio increases the market value of ESG stocks by $0.8.

title: Machine Learning Classification and Portfolio Construction: Does the Loss Function Matter?
From Models to Workflows: Communicating Agentic AI in Asset Management
Communicating Quantitative and AI-Driven Investment Strategies: Narrative, Interpretation, and Governance
Stakeholder Management and Communication in the Total Portfolio Approach
Explaining Risk to Boards: Translating Quantitative Models into Fiduciary Dialogue
SOTA: Stock Options Trading Agents Guided by Option-Implied Return Distributions
abstract: As option markets grow and AI advances, agentic systems for option trading are gaining increasing attention. Language-model-based agents can reason over contextual information such as news, but option trading presents a particularly challenging decision problem: a single stock can have thousands of contracts, and the agent must decide both which contracts to trade and how to combine them. Existing approaches often sidestep this complexity by restricting the policy to a fixed strategy structure, such as a straddle, limiting their ability to switch strategies as market conditions change. We present SOTA (Stock Options Trading Agents), an agentic trading framework for structured option-strategy selection. SOTA abstracts the large option universe into strategy-level decisions while deterministic resolvers handle portfolio implementation. We develop SOTA by post-training Qwen3.8-27B with supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning. SOTA is evaluated on options on nine large-cap U.S. equities and SPY against rule-based and machine-learning strategy selectors in the same trading environment. Over a six-month out-of-sample period, SOTA earns an 18.3% total return with a Sharpe ratio of 1.60 and a maximum drawdown of 8.96%. We also document an asymmetric role of news: news improves frontier-teacher trajectories, but retaining news during reinforcement learning reduces out-of-sample return from 18.3% to -2.7%.
summary: As option markets grow and AI advances, agentic systems for option trading are gaining increasing attention.
finding: We also document an asymmetric role of news: news improves frontier-teacher trajectories, but retaining news during reinforcement learning reduces out-of-sample return from 18.3% to -2.7%.

title: Effect Of Share Repurchase Programs on Shareholder Wealth: A Systematic Literature Review
publisher: Minnesota Journal of Business Law and Entrepreneurship
venue: Minnesota Journal of Business Law and Entrepreneurship
abstract: Stock buybacks, or share repurchase programs, are a corporate financial tool that has been an increasingly significant and influential financial approach to maximising shareholder wealth and capital allocation. The trend in firms in both developed and emerging economies over the last few decades has been that the companies have favoured repurchases to the traditional dividend payouts because it is more flexible, more effective in terms of taxes, and may lead to better earnings per share (EPS) and market value. The paper provides a systematic literature review of how share repurchase programs impact on shareholder wealth by providing a synthesis of key theoretical and empirical work published between 2000 and 2026. The PRISMA framework is used to ensure that the relevant studies are selected in a structured and transparent manner in the leading databases like Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar and the ScienceDirect. The results show that buyback announcements tend to have a positive short-term abnormal return which are indicative of positive investor responses and reflective of the effects. But the long-term evidence of shareholder wealth creation is still mixed and varies on the basis of undervaluation, financial position, quality of governance, market environment and the objective of repurchases. Another important effect of buybacks as indicated in the review is the enhancement of EPS, the optimisation of capital structure, reduction of agency cost, and the replacement of dividends. Besides, periods of crisis, like the Global Financial Crisis and the COVID-19 pandemic, made substantial impacts on the behaviour of repurchase. Generally, the research finds that share buyback programs can boost stockholder wealth provided they are adopted in a strategic manner and in combination with good corporate fundamentals. The paper has contributed to the literature by defining research gaps and providing future direction of the researchers, investors, managers and policymakers.
summary: Stock buybacks, or share repurchase programs, are a corporate financial tool that has been an increasingly significant and influential financial approach to maximising shareholder wealth and capital allocation.
finding: The results show that buyback announcements tend to have a positive short-term abnormal return which are indicative of positive investor responses and reflective of the effects.

title: Pricing Repurchase Promises: Expected Execution and Investor Beliefs
abstract: I study how investors price expected repurchase delivery and what actual purchases reveal beyond that expectation. Using 10,752 Chinese announcements, I construct an expanding out-of-sample execution forecast from current firm and plan information and distinguish it from historical execution reputation. Expected Execution predicts announcement returns beyond the earlier record, while a matched comparison associates authorizations with an additional immediate response following similar price declines. Execution relative to its forecast predicts later returns and earnings news; a disclosure-aligned comparison places public implementation information before the earnings releases. Around the Kangmei judgment, an external increase in disclosure liability, the forecast's pricing weight declines relatively more among firms without a public directors' and officers' insurance record. The evidence connects the value investors assign to a discretionary payout promise with delivery relative to expectation and with the accountability attached to the statement: credibility depends on what the current plan is expected to deliver, what subsequent conduct reveals, and how much corroboration the legal environment requires. JEL Classification: D83; G14; G35; G38
summary: Using 10,752 Chinese announcements, I construct an expanding out-of-sample execution forecast from current firm and plan information and distinguish it from historical execution reputation.
finding: I study how investors price expected repurchase delivery and what actual purchases reveal beyond that expectation.

title: Financial mismatch and stock mispricing in China: Industry-year averages and firm-level differences
Directing the Labor Market: Shared Directors and Employee Flows
abstract: Abstract Using résumé data on over 20 million U.S. workers, we find that the flow of employees between a pair of firms sharply drops by about 20% during periods in which the firms share a board director. This relationship is stronger in settings where firms have greater potential gains from limiting worker mobility and is most pronounced for higher-skilled employees. Moreover, we find more connected firms have lower rates of internal promotion and no improvements in employee satisfaction. The evidence is consistent with shared directors serving as a mechanism for labor market coordination.
summary: Using résumé data on over 20 million U.S. workers, we find that the flow of employees between a pair of firms sharply drops by about 20% during periods in which the firms share a board director.
finding: Moreover, we find more connected firms have lower rates of internal promotion and no improvements in employee satisfaction.

title: Central Bank Economic Transparency and Managerial Learning
abstract: Abstract Central banks increasingly disclose their private information regarding the economy’s current and future state (CBET). Consistent with CBET shifting investors’ collection and pricing of aggregate-level (where managers do not have an information advantage) toward firm-level (where managers do have an information advantage) information, we find that CBET reduces managers’ learning from stock price. The results are (1) pronounced when firms do not provide guidance and when noise trading in firms’ stock is low, and (2) robust to using the 2013–2014 amendments to the Bank of England’s Inflation Report as an exogenous shock. Additional evidence suggests that CBET lowers investment efficiency.
summary: Central banks increasingly disclose their private information regarding the economy’s current and future state (CBET).
finding: Consistent with CBET shifting investors’ collection and pricing of aggregate-level (where managers do not have an information advantage) toward firm-level (where managers do have an information advantage) information, we find that CBET reduces managers’…

title: Getting Bonds (and Diversification) Wrong
abstract: One of the most common views expressed in financial markets at present seems to be that bonds (particularly the government variety) are no longer an effective diversifier when held alongside equities in a multi-asset portfolio. These arguments are usually accompanied by a chart displaying rising stock and bond correlations, and perhaps some five-year performance numbers showing how poor fixed income returns have been. I think these perspectives get a lot wrong about the purpose of diversification and how bonds are behaving. Bonds are doing bond things If I had been told at the start of 2021 that over the coming years there would be several supply-side inflation shocks, substantial fiscal stimulus, inflation consistently above target and a material rise in interest rates – would I have been bearish on bonds? Even as someone who is reticent to make predictions, I am pretty sure I would have been – particularly starting from such unattractive valuations. The performance of bonds – and their changing relationship with equities – has been just what we would have expected given the starting conditions and subsequent environment. It is odd that an asset class behaving in a way that is entirely consistent with its structural features is a reason to abandon it, or suggest it is not working. Bonds seem to be working just fine. Unfortunately, all asset classes are vulnerable to a particular set of circumstances, and the precise timing of those circumstances is usually well beyond our capabilities. This is why we diversify. Starting valuations matter The valuation of bonds matters a huge amount to their expected future returns, and it is also vital to their diversifying properties. Higher starting yields provide strong insulation from losses incurred due to rising yield levels, offer greater scope for yields to fall during downturns and provide better long-term returns in the unknowable future paths that lie ahead of us. Valuations are not just about headline yields (inflation matters a lot too), but lots of pessimistic takes on bonds seem wilfully oblivious to the fact that higher starting real and nominal yields are a good thing for investors. Don’t judge an asset class by its (short-term) performance The powerful narrative around the ineffectiveness of bonds is classic investor behaviour. We take recent returns, build a story to explain them and then extrapolate. Using the same process to describe bonds as broken now would lead us to be incredibly bullish in 2020 – they had performed remarkably well in prior years and exhibited a negative correlation with equities, what was not to like? (Apart from valuations that is, but who cares about those?) An approach to diversification that relies on the performance profile of an asset class through a particular period or ‘regime’ is inevitably deeply flawed. Diversification is about building a portfolio for a range of future paths that are at best uncertain and at worst entirely unknowable. Making allocation decis
summary: One of the most common views expressed in financial markets at present seems to be that bonds (particularly the government variety) are no longer an effective diversifier when held alongside equities in a multi-asset portfolio.
finding: We take recent returns, build a story to explain them and then extrapolate.

title: Inflation, DER, PER, and TATO as Determinants of Capital Gains for Indonesian Telecommunication Companies (2020-2025)
venue: JOURNAL OF HUMANITIES SOCIAL SCIENCES AND BUSINESS (JHSSB)
abstract: Telecommunications sector stocks are widely regarded as stable, defensive investments, attractive to investors due to consistent capital gains and reliable dividend yields. Financial performance across major operators shows revenue growth, though accompanied by rising operational costs driven by network investment and corporate actions, while growth of the digital economy and demand for internet data continue to drive capital gains. Focusing on ten telecommunications companies over the 2020–2025 period, this study explores how capital gains are shaped by the Debt-to-Equity Ratio (DER), the Price-Earnings Ratio (PER), Total Asset Turnover (TATO), and the inflation rate. A panel data regression framework was employed, with model selection guided by the Chow, Hausman, and Lagrange Multiplier procedures, alongside classical assumption testing to confirm that the estimates were consistent, unbiased, and precise. The results indicate that inflation negatively and significantly affects capital gains, while DER, PER, and TATO are all positively and significantly associated with capital gains in partial analyses. Jointly, these four predictors explain 9% of the variance in capital gains and exert a collectively significant influence. Because telecommunications stocks often experience price swings, fundamental analysis remains vital for determining true share value and appraising business fundamentals, beyond what short-term price actions reveal. Asset values are further shaped by infrastructure expansion, including fiber-optic networks, base transceiver stations, and data centers, as well as by capital structure and leverage, which influence firm value. Between 2020 and 2025, inflation in Indonesia remained relatively stable, though its rise contributed to higher operating costs and profit stagnation.
summary: Telecommunications sector stocks are widely regarded as stable, defensive investments, attractive to investors due to consistent capital gains and reliable dividend yields.
finding: Jointly, these four predictors explain 9% of the variance in capital gains and exert a collectively significant influence.

title: The Macroeconomics of Irrational Exuberance, Mathematical Microstructures of the VIX, and Prospect Theory: A Behavioral and Empirical Synthesis
abstract: This paper investigates the cyclical architecture of asset price bubbles and the behavioral microstructures that accelerate systemic market panics. By contextualizing historical market disruptions ranging from 17th-century European speculative manias to modern systemic failures, we evaluate how positive "price-to-price" feedback loops transform into rapid, emotionally driven liquidation cascades. This paper explicitly integrates the mathematical framework of the Cboe Volatility Index (VIX) model-free variance formulation with Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky’s Prospect Theory value function. By mapping cognitive biases— specifically loss aversion and non-linear probability weighting—to options-implied variance, we demonstrate how asymmetric individual risk evaluation aggregates into macro-level liquidity squeezes. Finally, we evaluate systematic quantitative risk-targeting protocols and discretionary portfolio hedging overlays as necessary mechanisms to defend institutional capital against procyclical reflexivity loops.
summary: This paper investigates the cyclical architecture of asset price bubbles and the behavioral microstructures that accelerate systemic market panics.
finding: Finally, we evaluate systematic quantitative risk-targeting protocols and discretionary portfolio hedging overlays as necessary mechanisms to defend institutional capital against procyclical reflexivity loops.

title: Investor attention and GCC stock market connectedness during the first wave of COVID-19: evidence using Google trends and VIX
abstract: Purpose This study investigates the behavioral determinants of financial market connectedness in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) during the first wave of COVID-19. It examines whether the Chicago Board Options Exchange Volatility Index (VIX), regional investor attention measured via Google Trends, and their interaction are associated with changes in connectedness. Design/methodology/approach Time-varying parameter vector autoregression (TVP-VAR) is used to estimate the Total Connectedness Index (TCI) across GCC stock markets from (2018–2022). Moreover, behavioral regressions over the first wave (January–August 2020) assess the role of VIX, Google Trends-based regional attention (GTR), and their interaction. Findings TCI nearly doubled from 31.94% during the pre-COVID period to 64.25% throughout the crisis. After controlling for oil volatility, neither VIX nor GTR was significant. Notwithstanding, their interaction is positive and statistically significant, nearly doubling the model's explanatory power. Given fundamental controls, Granger causality tests show unidirectional precedence from GTR to TCI in bivariate specifications. Results hold despite the exclusion of March 2020 and the addition of COVID-19 case growth. Originality/value This study integrates TVP-VAR connectedness with behavioral finance theory in GCC markets. Crucially, it introduces Google Trends as a regional attention measure, and documents an attention–uncertainty interaction consistent with behavioral amplification through which connectedness intensifies when both channels are simultaneously elevated.
summary: This study investigates the behavioral determinants of financial market connectedness in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) during the first wave of COVID-19.
finding: Given fundamental controls, Granger causality tests show unidirectional precedence from GTR to TCI in bivariate specifications.

title: The Rise of Finfluencers and Their Impact on Individual Investment Decisions in India: A Regulatory Perspective with Reference to SEBI Guidelines
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Abstract: The rapid rise of financial influencers popularly known as finfluencers has been one of the most visible developments in India’s financial ecosystem in the last decade. Social media platforms such as YouTube, Instagram, Telegram, Reddit, Facebook and X (formally known Twitter) have provided ordinary individuals with an opportunity to present investment-related content to mass audiences. As India has witnessed full exponential growth and flowering in retail participation in the stock market and mutual funds. Finfluencers have emerged as a crucial bridge between formal financial institutions and young digitally-savvy investors. By providing simplified complex financial decisions they contribute to financial inclusion and digital literacy where formal financial education remains limited. However, their growing influence has also raised significant regulatory, ethical, and economic concerns. The absence of mandatory registration, instances of biased or sponsored recommendations, and the amplification of behavioral biases have created new challenges for investor protection. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has in response proposed and implemented multiple guidelines since 2023 to address this phenomenon. These include restrictions on intermediaries’ partnerships with finfluencers, mandatory disclosures for paid promotions, and warnings against unregistered advisory services. This research is based exclusively on secondary data that critically examines the rise of finfluencers in India and their implications for individual investment decision-making & SEBI’s regulatory stance. From academic literature, regulatory reports, media coverage, and expert commentaries the paper provides a holistic understanding of the dual role finfluencers play in democratizing finance and exposing retail investors to new risks. It also situates SEBI’s interventions in a comparative global context by drawing parallels with measures adopted by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and the UK’s Financial Conduct Authority (FCA). The findings highlight a regulatory dilemma: how to strike a balance between protecting investors from misleading advice while not stifling the positive role of finfluencers in enhancing financial awareness. The study concludes with policy recommendations, enhanced investor education, platform-level accountability, and adaptive regulatory mechanisms to ensure sustainable financial innovation.
summary: The rapid rise of financial influencers popularly known as finfluencers has been one of the most visible developments in India’s financial ecosystem in the last decade.
finding: However, their growing influence has also raised significant regulatory, ethical, and economic concerns.

title: Creation after destruction? Financial intermediation and firm entry after bank cleanups
abstract: Abstract We study a large and unanticipated bank cleanup in India after prolonged zombie lending under regulatory forbearance. The cleanup forced widespread zombie exits through bankruptcy. In contrast to a frictionless world where entry automatically follows exit, we show that with financial frictions, local banking conditions shape creation after destruction. New firm entry occurs primarily in regions where banks are present, well-capitalized, competitive, and possess sectoral expertise. We further find a decline in the dispersion of total factor productivity in regions with stronger financial intermediation, consistent with a reduction in misallocation in such areas.
summary: We study a large and unanticipated bank cleanup in India after prolonged zombie lending under regulatory forbearance.
finding: We further find a decline in the dispersion of total factor productivity in regions with stronger financial intermediation, consistent with a reduction in misallocation in such areas.

title: An Open Letter: The Architecture of a Data-Driven National OS and Circular Capitalism
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: The current global economy operates on the premise of infinite linear growth within a finite physical environment, inevitably leading to the expansion of fictional capital (speculative bubbles) disconnected from the real economy. To prevent the loss of social infrastructure and technological assets caused by catastrophic market crashes, this paper proposes a state-led "Graceful Shutdown" model, applying the systems engineering concept of "Garbage Collection" (GC) to macroeconomic policy. Specifically, it introduces a controlled liquidation process where a detection mechanism flags "meaningless speculative stock purchases" devoid of physical or informational output, allowing the central bank to use its root authority to gradually buy back and safely erase (return to the soil) these overvalued assets from the ledger. Crucially, to prevent political arbitrage and crony capitalism, the detection and liquidation algorithms are fully open-source and deterministically executed. The system dynamically optimizes itself—much like a compiler refining code execution—by feeding back new macroeconomic indicators, such as the Information Fork Rate and System Load Average, replacing obsolete metrics like GDP. During this orchestrated soft landing, the true assets of obsolete industries—technological data, operational know-how, and infrastructure—are salvaged and integrated into a state-managed, open-source data repository. The transition to a "Data-Driven Circular Capitalism"—neutralizing fictional capital back into the soil and redistributing extracted pure information resources as seeds for new creation—is the cornerstone of the next-generation National OS architecture.
summary: The current global economy operates on the premise of infinite linear growth within a finite physical environment, inevitably leading to the expansion of fictional capital (speculative bubbles) disconnected from the real economy.
finding: The transition to a "Data-Driven Circular Capitalism"—neutralizing fictional capital back into the soil and redistributing extracted pure information resources as seeds for new creation—is the cornerstone of the next-generation National OS architecture.

title: Construction Rules for the Morningstar® PitchBook Listed Private Equity IndexSM Family
EVALUATION OF SHARI'AH STOCKS INTEGRATING TOTAL RETURN AND MARGIN OF SAFETY: EVIDENCE FROM THE JAKARTA ISLAMIC INDEX 2020–2025
publisher: Currency Jurnal Ekonomi dan Perbankan Syariah
venue: Currency Jurnal Ekonomi dan Perbankan Syariah
abstract: This research is motivated by the development of the Islamic capital market in Indonesia and investors' need for investment evaluation methods that measure not only the level of return but also the level of investment safety. Most previous studies tend to analyze Islamic stock returns and stock valuations separately, thus failing to provide a comprehensive overview of investment quality. This study aims to analyze the level of investment return through Total Return, the level of investment safety through Margin of Safety (MOS), and the relationship between these two indicators in high-dividend Shari'ah stocks included in the Jakarta Islamic Index (JII) for the 2020–2025 period. The study employs a quantitative approach with a descriptive-comparative design and Spearman correlation analysis on 11 stocks that met the sampling criteria. Total Return is calculated based on capital gains and dividend yields, while the Margin of Safety is determined through intrinsic value estimation using the Graham Number method. The results indicate that ADRO generated the highest Total Return at 229.43%, while INDF had the highest Margin of Safety at 56.37%. The analysis also identified six undervalued stocks and five overvalued stocks. The Spearman correlation test yielded a coefficient of 0.627 with a significance value of 0.039, indicating a positive and significant relationship between Total Return and Margin of Safety. These findings confirm that integrating income investing and value investing approaches can provide a more comprehensive evaluation of Islamic stock investments for investors.
summary: This research is motivated by the development of the Islamic capital market in Indonesia and investors' need for investment evaluation methods that measure not only the level of return but also the level of investment safety.
finding: The Spearman correlation test yielded a coefficient of 0.627 with a significance value of 0.039, indicating a positive and significant relationship between Total Return and Margin of Safety.

title: Bad news travels fast: comment letters, investor trading behavior, and stock liquidity
abstract: Purpose This study investigates the effect of real-time disclosed regulatory comment letters on corporate stock liquidity and explores the underlying driving factors, using a unique sample from the Chinese stock market. Leveraging the timely nature of comment letter issuance and the subsequent reply mechanism in China, the paper aims to unambiguously identify the market consequences of comment letters and the associated mechanisms. Specifically, we focus on the role of different investor groups' trading behaviors, particularly retail net-sells and investor sentiment, in mediating the liquidity changes. Ultimately, this research provides new insights into the market monitoring effect of comment letters and regulatory enforcement in emerging markets. Design/methodology/approach We manually collected a sample of comment letters and their real-time replies issued by the Shenzhen Stock Exchange (SZSE) from 2014 to 2018. We employ event study methodology and Difference-in-Differences (DiD) models to analyze the changes in inquired firms' stock liquidity, measured by the Quoted Spread (QS) and Effective Spread (ES), following the comment letter disclosure. We proxy retail investor trading behavior using net sell volumes of small transactions and examine the driving role of retail net-sells and negative retail sentiment in the observed liquidity decline. This design leverages the unique institutional setting of real-time disclosure in the Chinese market. Findings The findings demonstrate that the stock liquidity of inquired firms significantly declines immediately after the comment letter disclosure. However, this decline does not significantly recover after the firms issue their subsequent replies. The short-term deterioration in liquidity is mainly driven by intense retail net-selling activities and heightened negative retail sentiment. Furthermore, the liquidity exhibits only a partial recovery over a longer period, extending up to 60 days post-disclosure. Finally, the negative effect of comment letters on stock liquidity is more pronounced for firms characterized by higher information uncertainty and greater corporate governance deficiencies. Originality/value This study uses the real-time disclosure mechanism of comment letters in the Chinese market to examine their impact on the trading behavior of different investor groups, particularly retail investors, thus mitigating concerns about insider trading. It confirms a significant regulatory effect of comment letters as a non-punitive regulatory tool in the capital market, filling a gap in the literature regarding their efficacy. By focusing on the unique emerging market context of China, this research enriches the global understanding of comment letters' impact and offers important practical implications for improving regulatory instruments worldwide.
summary: This study investigates the effect of real-time disclosed regulatory comment letters on corporate stock liquidity and explores the underlying driving factors, using a unique sample from the Chinese stock market.
finding: It confirms a significant regulatory effect of comment letters as a non-punitive regulatory tool in the capital market, filling a gap in the literature regarding their efficacy.

title: Cost of Capital and Capital Structure of Oberoi Realty Limited: A Five-Year Analysis and Peer Benchmarking
venue: INTERANTIONAL JOURNAL OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT
abstract: In this research paper, the cost of capital of Oberoi Realty Limited, an Indian real estate developer, has been evaluated through quantitative descriptive case study. This study analyzes the company financial data collected in the provided research materials for financial years 2021-22 to 2025-26 and estimates weighted average cost of capital (WACC) for FY2025-26. In this paper, analysis includes revenue, finance cost, profit after tax, borrowings and equity, cost of debt from borrowings interest and average borrowings, cost of equity from Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM), and finally, combining both using capital weights. Considering a risk-free rate of 6.96%, beta of 0.66 and equity risk premium of 7.00%, cost of equity has been estimated at 11.58%. Estimated pre-tax cost of debt is 7.62% while after-tax is 5.83%. Using market value equity and book borrowings as debt, estimated indicative WACC is approximately 11.28%. Sensitivity analysis suggests that WACC lies approximately between 10.97% and 11.60% with variation in equity risk premium between 6.50% and 7.50%. From the results, it can be said that estimate is largely influenced by equity as it constitutes about 94.82% of capital base used. The results provided are not company-reported but rather calculated based on assumptions made on market data and taxes.
summary: In this research paper, the cost of capital of Oberoi Realty Limited, an Indian real estate developer, has been evaluated through quantitative descriptive case study.
finding: The results provided are not company-reported but rather calculated based on assumptions made on market data and taxes.

title: Cost of Capital and Capital Structure of Page Industries Ltd.: A Five-Year Analysis
venue: INTERANTIONAL JOURNAL OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT
abstract: Our research problem is the cost of capital and capital structure of Page Industries Limited. Annual reports and market data will be used to find context for the cost of capital and capital structure in corporate finance. This case study will cover FY 2021–22 to FY 2025–26. We will use key financial measures, which are revenue, profitability, efficiency, finance costs, return on net worth, and the debt-to-equity ratio. We will use the cost of capital in the context of corporate finance theory as well as the company’s financial performance. The formula used to calculate the cost of equity in FY 2025–26 is the Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM). In this method, cost of equity = risk-free rate of interest + β (equity risk premium). The risk-free rate of interest = 6.96%, β = 0.67, and the equity risk premium = 7.00%. The cost of equity, calculated in this way, is approximately 11.65%. Since the calculated capital structure was based on the fair value of the assets, the weighted average cost of capital is calculated to be approximately 11.61% using the lease-based proxy cost of debt. This demonstrates that the article proposes there is no significant use of external financing. The capital structure is therefore more traditional. The investigation compares Page Industries with Lux Industries and Dollar Industries. Page Industries is more profitable, and peer companies differ in their leverage and capital structures. Accordingly, companies should maintain financial flexibility, manage leases, and make investments at the right cost of capital. [4, 9, 10, 11, 13, 14, 15, 18, 19, 20, 21, 23]
summary: Our research problem is the cost of capital and capital structure of Page Industries Limited.
finding: This demonstrates that the article proposes there is no significant use of external financing.

title: Cost of Capital and Capital Structure of Kalyan Jewellers India Ltd.: A Five-Year Analysis
venue: INTERANTIONAL JOURNAL OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT
abstract: The paper seeks to analyze the cost of capital and capital structure of Kalyan Jewellers India Limited, one of the biggest organized jewellery retailers in India, for the five years ending 31 March 2025. Based on annual reports of the company and other sources, the analysis looks into the evolution of revenue, profitability and leverage during the period under review and the estimation of cost of equity for FY2025-26 by means of the Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM). With a risk-free rate of 6.87%, a beta of 1.40 and an equity risk premium of 7.00%, the cost of equity for FY2025-26 comes to about 16.67%. Taking this together with a pre-tax cost of debt of about 8.0% (comprising borrowing in connection with gold-metal-loans and leases) and an effective tax rate of 25.1%, the WACC based on market-value weights, wherein equity represents about 87% of capital, becomes about 15.3%. Unlike Page Industries or any other equity intensive consumer company, the proportion of working-capital debt (mainly gold metal loan) of Kalyan Jewellers is significantly higher compared to that of equity. Kalyan Jewellers is being compared with two other organised jewellery retailers in the form of Senco Gold Limited and Thangamayil Jewellery Limited. The comparative analysis reveals that Kalyan Jewellers has emerged as the biggest company in terms of revenue generation but not as the most profitable in margin terms, with Senco Gold emerging as the leader in PAT margin in FY2025-26 owing to gold price led increase in inventory value.
summary: The paper seeks to analyze the cost of capital and capital structure of Kalyan Jewellers India Limited, one of the biggest organized jewellery retailers in India, for the five years ending 31 March 2025.
finding: Unlike Page Industries or any other equity intensive consumer company, the proportion of working-capital debt (mainly gold metal loan) of Kalyan Jewellers is significantly higher compared to that of equity.

title: Capital Structure, Cost of Capital, and Value Creation: An Empirical Study
venue: INTERANTIONAL JOURNAL OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT
abstract: In the highly leveraged world of auto manufacturing, taking on debt is usually just part of the game. But Bosch Limited, a heavyweight tier-1 automotive supplier listed on both the NSE and BSE, plays by a very different set of rules. This paper delivers the financial playbook of Bosch, exploring how the company structures its capital, prices it, and ultimately translates those choices into real shareholder value. By digging through five years of audited standalone financials (FY 2021-22 to FY 2025-26), we set to see if Bosch's strictly zero-debt approach actually holds up when pitted against traditional corporate finance theories. To put some hard numbers behind this strategy, we used the Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM) and the Weighted Average Cost of Capital (WACC) to figure out the company's true hurdle rate. The math simply confirms what anyone glancing at their balance sheet already suspects: Bosch is completely unlevered. With a debt-to-equity ratio of exactly 0.00x, equity carries the entire 100% weight. Plugging in a 7.10% risk-free rate, an adjusted beta of 0.85, and a 6.00% equity risk premium, both the cost of equity and the WACC settle right at 12.20%. It's a straightforward mathematical reality-when you have zero debt, your WACC is just your cost of equity. But does this conservative approach leave money on the table? To find out, we benchmarked Bosch against two industry peers: Schaeffler India and Samvardhana Motherson International. While these competitors use debt to lower their nominal WACC via interest tax shields, Bosch clearly prioritizes long-term solvency and operational flexibility. And the strategy is paying off. Bosch is generating a Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) of 21.54%. Since that easily clears their 12.20% WACC by a massive 9.34 percentage points, the company is creating a very healthy Economic Value Added (EVA) spread. Ultimately, this heavily equity-funded model is a clear real-world example of the Pecking Order Theory in action. More importantly, it gives Bosch the financial breathing room to fund its massive pivot toward electric mobility and softwaredefined vehicles. By avoiding the heavy debt loads that trap others during industry slumps, Bosch has positioned itself to navigate the auto sector's inevitable cyclical downturns without taking on dangerous levels of financial risk.
summary: In the highly leveraged world of auto manufacturing, taking on debt is usually just part of the game.
finding: While these competitors use debt to lower their nominal WACC via interest tax shields, Bosch clearly prioritizes long-term solvency and operational flexibility.

title: Cost of Capital Analysis:Avenue Supermarts
venue: INTERANTIONAL JOURNAL OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT
abstract: The Weighted Average Cost of Capital (WACC) is determined by estimates of the cost of equity, after-tax cost of debt and weights of the capital structure. These inputs are based on information provided in audited disclosures and industry benchmarks and capital market data. Avenue Supermarts is operating with a debt-capital structure, thus its WACC will be solely a function of the cost of equity. The company's cost of capital for FY24 is estimated at around 11.05% as per Capital Asset Pricing Model or CAPM, a mere 20 bps higher than the previous fiscal year 2020. This cost is very consistent over the period 2020 to 2024. The stability of this rating is due to the company's low beta of 0.41, which is in line with peers in the domestic retail sector. This cost of capital advantage of 60- to 180-bps is determined by comparing with other listed retail domestic companies in a -sectional analysis. Even though debt Ave Supermarts doesn't use debt, it has a lower cost of capital than many of its competitors. The range of the companys Return on Invested Capital or ROIC is between 18% and 20%, putting the company 700 to 900 basis points above the hurdle rate. The robust spread backs company's investments in its physical stores and the automated logistics systems. Capital decision trade-offs are made between flexibility of a free structure and the tax advantages of debt financing when assessing the company's capital options.
summary: The Weighted Average Cost of Capital (WACC) is determined by estimates of the cost of equity, after-tax cost of debt and weights of the capital structure.
finding: Even though debt Ave Supermarts doesn't use debt, it has a lower cost of capital than many of its competitors.

title: Financial Performance and Board Structure Valuation: A Study
venue: INTERANTIONAL JOURNAL OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT
abstract: This paper studies financial performance, corporate governance, agency problems and business ethics at Exide Industries Limited over FY2020–21 to FY2024–25. Exide is a relevant Unit I case because its battery business combines manufacturing risk, lead sourcing and recycling, energy-transition exposure, product responsibility, safety obligations and a substantial public shareholder base. The study uses a documentary, longitudinal case-study approach based on Exide’s integrated annual reports, audited financial statements, corporate-governance report, BRSR, CSR disclosures, statutory material and a peer benchmark with Amara Raja Energy & Mobility Limited. Exide’s standalone sales increased from ₹10,041 crore in FY2020–21 to ₹16,588 crore in FY2024–25, while operating profit rose from ₹1,356 crore to ₹1,893 crore. The sales endpoint CAGR was 13.37%; operating-profit CAGR was 8.70%. In FY2024–25 the company reported an 11.4% operating margin, 6.49% net margin, 1.51 current ratio and 0.03 debt-equity ratio. The governance profile showed four independent directors out of seven (57.14%) and promoter holding of 45.99%. The study concludes that Exide has strong formal processes and a conservative balance sheet, while Board-level transparency should focus more on capital allocation, technology transition, related-party oversight and measurable remediation.
summary: This paper studies financial performance, corporate governance, agency problems and business ethics at Exide Industries Limited over FY2020–21 to FY2024–25.
finding: The governance profile showed four independent directors out of seven (57.14%) and promoter holding of 45.99%.

title: Investor Sentiment and Tech-Sector Stock Returns: An Empirical Analysis Based on Guba Comment Volume
abstract: Purpose - This study investigates whether investor sentiment carries causal information about the future returns of five large-cap Chinese technology stocks. Design/methodology/approach - High-frequency proxies for sentiment are built from the daily count of emotion-tagged posts on Guba and from daily return metrics. After cross-sectional correlation and ADF stationarity checks, two-stage residual regressions and pooled panel specifications with lagged sentiment terms are estimated. The sample is then split into training and validation windows; out-of-sample forecasts are benchmarked against the Efficient-Market-Hypothesis (EMH) null. Finally, mean–variance frontiers that blend the five equities with Chinese government bonds are constructed to obtain implementable portfolio weights. Findings - Non-contemporaneous sentiment exerts a statistically and economically significant effect on next-day returns. Both the residual and pooled models deliver out-of-sample MSPEs that are materially lower than the EMH benchmark. Incorporating sentiment-adjusted expected returns shifts the efficient frontier north-west, yielding higher Sharpe ratios. Originality - The paper is the first to fuse intraday social-media emotion data with conventional econometric tests of predictability for Chinese technology firms, and to show that sentiment-driven return forecasts can be translated into realizable portfolio allocations.
summary: Purpose - This study investigates whether investor sentiment carries causal information about the future returns of five large-cap Chinese technology stocks.
finding: Originality - The paper is the first to fuse intraday social-media emotion data with conventional econometric tests of predictability for Chinese technology firms, and to show that sentiment-driven return forecasts can be translated into realizable portfolio…

Navigating Geoeconomic Risk in the U.S. Stock Market
abstract: Matteo Crosignani, Lina Han, and Marco Macchiavelli Geoeconomic risk—the risk that firms incur valuation losses when countries deploy economic, trade, or financial leverage for geopolitical aims—has become a first-order concern for investors. In this post, based on our recent Staff Report , we document that domestic U.S. stocks expose investors to substantial geoeconomic risk through firms’ global supply-chain relationships, affecting investors’ returns and portfolio allocation. We also find that investors are compensated for bearing geoeconomic risk through higher risk premia. Export Controls as Geoeconomic Shocks Investors do not need to own foreign stocks to be exposed to geoeconomic risk. Domestic stocks can embed foreign exposures when U.S. firms sell to overseas customers or rely on global supply chains. These links mean that a foreign policy shock can reduce the value of U.S.-listed firms and transmit geoeconomic risk to domestic portfolios. These global links can help investors diversify their portfolios when shocks are country- or –market-specific, but they offer less protection when policy shocks affect the same international relationships across many U.S. firms. Geoeconomic shocks are therefore difficult to diversify away because they can affect multiple domestic stocks through a common foreign exposure. We study this risk through the imposition of U.S. export controls by the Bureau of Industry and Security. This agency of the Department of Commerce can restrict U.S. firms from selling certain technologies to specific foreign entities deemed to be a risk to U.S. national security. Since 2014, these restrictions have been leveraged frequently in the U.S.-China technological rivalry, especially in industries such as semiconductors, telecommunications, artificial intelligence, and advanced computing. We interpret the addition of a foreign firm to the export control list as a manifestation of geoeconomic risk for its U.S. suppliers. This setting lets us trace geoeconomic risk from targeted Chinese firms to U.S. investors. We hand-collect Chinese entities added to U.S. export-control lists and use FactSet Revere supply-chain data to identify the U.S. suppliers connected to these directly targeted Chinese customers. We then match those affected U.S. suppliers to the holdings of U.S. domestic equity mutual funds from the CRSP Mutual Fund Database, covering more than 5,000 funds from 2010 to 2023. We focus on mutual funds because they are major investors in U.S. equity markets: long-term mutual funds held around a fifth of U.S. corporate equity in 2025. In addition, thanks to their monthly portfolio holdings, we observe which funds owned U.S. suppliers to newly targeted Chinese firms when export controls are announced, and to track how managers rebalance their portfolios afterward. title: Quarterly Review: Cautious Investors Tap the Brakes
Research on Estimation Methods of Key Parameters and Model Robustness of Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) in Financial Modeling
publisher: European Journal of Business Economics & Management
venue: European Journal of Business Economics & Management
abstract: Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) modeling remains a cornerstone of corporate valuation, yet its practical reliability hinges critically on the accuracy and stability of key input parameters—particularly the discount rate, terminal growth rate, and forecast horizon—and on the model’s resilience to parameter perturbations. This study systematically evaluates estimation methods for these parameters using both theoretical derivation and empirical simulation across diverse industry sectors and capital structures. We implement a multi-scenario Monte Carlo framework to quantify sensitivity, error propagation, and robustness thresholds under stochastic assumptions about cost of capital, reinvestment efficiency, and macroeconomic volatility. Our analysis reveals that conventional CAPM-based discount rate estimation introduces median valuation errors exceeding 22% when equity risk premiums deviate by ±150 bps; in contrast, a hybrid build-up approach incorporating firm-specific credit spreads and sectoral beta adjustments reduces error dispersion by 43%. Terminal growth rate estimation proves most vulnerable: a 0.25% deviation from sustainable long-term GDP plus inflation yields median absolute valuation shifts of 37%, with compounded sensitivity increasing exponentially beyond 2.8% in mature industries. Robustness testing demonstrates that models calibrated using rolling five-year beta windows and dynamic terminal multiples exhibit 61% higher stability under market shifts than static single-period benchmarks. Crucially, we identify a non-linear interaction effect: parameter uncertainty is not additive but multiplicative, meaning small errors in both discount and growth rates jointly degrade valuation fidelity more severely than either alone. These findings provide actionable methodological refinements for practitioners and underscore the necessity of embedding parameter uncertainty directly into DCF output reporting—not as footnotes, but as integral confidence bands.
summary: Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) modeling remains a cornerstone of corporate valuation, yet its practical reliability hinges critically on the accuracy and stability of key input parameters—particularly the discount rate, terminal growth rate, and forecast horizon—and on the model’s resilience to parameter perturbations.
finding: Robustness testing demonstrates that models calibrated using rolling five-year beta windows and dynamic terminal multiples exhibit 61% higher stability under market shifts than static single-period benchmarks.

title: Financial results management of industrial enterprises: an integrated approach to risk management and performance assessment
publisher: Economic Bulletin of Dnipro University of Technology
venue: Economic Bulletin of Dnipro University of Technology
abstract: Methods. Scientific results and applied developments were obtained through the application of a set of general scientific and specialized methods of cognition: system-structural and functional analysis – to substantiate the architecture of an integrated system for managing the financial results of industrial enterprises and structure its components; matrix modeling (RACI model) – for the functional allocation of authority, responsibility zones, and optimization of cross-departmental interaction; strategic time decomposition – to formulate a roadmap and prioritize stabilization measures across time horizons; the indicator method and target-oriented approach – to construct a balanced system of key performance indicators (KPIs) to verify liquidity, profitability, and return on investment; risk management and matrix identification methods – to systematize exogenous and endogenous threats and substantiate mechanisms for their mitigation and hedging; tabular and graphical generalization – to formalize relationships and visualize analytical data. Results. The conceptual foundations for forming an integrated system of financial results management for industrial enterprises have been substantiated, drawing upon the synergy of financial management, multifaceted diversification, operational risk management, and innovative development. A multi-level matrix of authority and responsibility allocation based on the RACI framework was developed, formalizing the interaction of key departments across responsibility centers and eliminating duplication of functions. An adaptive roadmap for implementing anti-crisis and stabilization measures was established, decomposing them into short-term (cost management, derivatives), medium-term (product-market diversification, asset optimization), and long-term (digitalization, ERP systems) initiatives. A set of aligned key performance indicators (KPIs) focused on monitoring operating margin, absolute liquidity, and return on invested capital was proposed, alongside a risk identification matrix specifying preventive mitigation tools and financial hedging instruments (forwards, futures, swaps). Novelty. The scientific novelty of the obtained results lies in the improvement of the organizational and economic mechanism for managing the financial results of industrial enterprises, which, unlike existing fragmented approaches, integrates functional role allocation using the RACI model, temporal structuring of stabilization measures, targeted operational performance evaluation via a balanced KPI system, and risk-oriented hedging of price and currency fluctuations into a unified adaptive management loop under conditions of dynamic market uncertainty. Practical value. The practical significance of the obtained results is that the developed provisions, matrices, and analytical tables provide an applied methodological foundation for designing internal corporate financial recovery programs, enhancing profitability, and increasing the operational efficiency of industrial entities. The application of the RACI matrix removes institutional barriers within corporate organizational structures, the KPI framework equips management with an effective instrument for monitoring and timely adjusting financial and sales policies, and the proposed roadmap enables the rational allocation of limited resources between immediate operational needs and strategic vectors of technological modernization.
